title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool & parallel calls with robust result injection and retry semantics
author: Aisha Patel
commits: initial: implement parallel executor and injection layer (wip)
fix: respect per-tool timeout and cancelation in executor
tests: add unit/integration tests for multi-tool parallel flows
docs: document new tool result injection order and retry semantics
chore: small refactor to openai_compat handler for backwards compatibility
description: Motivation: customers increasingly use multi-tool flows with parallel invocations and expect deterministic injection of tool results back into the model context plus resilient retries for transient tool failures. This PR improves execution ergonomics by introducing a parallel tool executor, deterministic injection ordering, configurable per-tool retry policies, and tighter OpenAI-compat behavior for legacy clients. Implementation summary: 1) Add services/runtime/tool_calling/executor.py: a lightweight parallel runner that schedules tool calls, enforces per-tool timeouts, supports cancellation hooks, and returns structured tool results. 2) Add services/runtime/tool_calling/injector.py: deterministic result injector that merges tool outputs into the conversation state using stable ordering rules and conflict resolution hints. 3) Extend openai_compat/handler.py to accept the new parallel_tools request shape, preserve backwards-compatible single-tool flow, and expose retry/backoff hints to clients. 4) SDK change (sdk/python/redwood/tooling.py): client helpers for specifying parallel tool groups and per-tool retry overrides. 5) Tests: unit tests for executor and injector plus integration tests that exercise transient failure, retry backoff, and result ordering. 6) Docs: updates to docs/tool-calling.md covering new API shape, examples, and recommended retry profiles. Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-1387) - [x] Implementation of executor+injector - [x] Unit tests for executor logic - [x] Integration tests for retries and injection - [x] Docs & examples updated - [x] CI passing Notes on semantics and compatibility: - Default behavior remains single-tool synchronous invocation when client sends legacy payloads to minimize risk. - New request field parallel_tools accepts an array of tool descriptors and an optional group_id; executor will issue calls concurrently up to a capped concurrency per-request (configurable in runtime config). - Deterministic injection: results are injected in order of tool descriptor index unless tools include explicit dependency metadata; injector exposes a conflict resolution policy (prefer-first, merge-json, custom-hook). - Retries: per-tool retry policy supports "none", "idempotent-only", "best-effort" with exponential backoff and jitter. Non-idempotent tools default to idempotent-only to avoid side-effect duplication. - Error handling: transient failures trigger retries according to policy; repeated failures surface structured error objects to the model as tool_result.error and do not crash the request. - OpenAI compat: openai_compat/handler maps legacy tool_calling responses to the new structured result shape to avoid breaking older clients. Performance/observability: executor emits per-tool latencies, retry counts, and cancellation metrics; added tracing spans for scheduling/injection to help diagnose ordering issues. Backwards compatibility: preserved. Rollout plan: feature flag gated (runtime flag: feature.tool_parallel_executor) enabled for canary, then wider rollout after metrics validation. Impact: reduces tail latency for multi-tool flows by parallelizing non-dependent tools and improves developer ergonomics around retries and deterministic injections. See tests and docs for examples.
review_comments: Jordan Kim: Please ensure per-tool timeouts are enforced as hard cancellations; in earlier runs we saw stray goroutines holding KV caches.
Aisha Patel (author): Implemented hard cancellation and added GC-safe hooks in executor. Added tests that assert cancellation frees related resources.
Elena Ruiz: The deterministic injection rules look good; recommend adding a note about merging conflicting JSON outputs in the docs.
Aisha Patel: Added 'merge-json' policy and example in docs/tool-calling.md.
Samir Desai: CI initially failed due to flaky test in tests/integration/test_tool_retries.py (race on simulated network). Re-ran CI after adding deterministic wait and the pipeline passed.
Jordan Kim: Approved after CI green and a small nit fixed in openai_compat mapping (preserve 'tool_id' field).
release_notes: Improved tool-calling ergonomics: parallel tool execution, deterministic result injection, per-tool retry policies with safe defaults, OpenAI-compat mapping preserved. Backwards compatible and gated by runtime feature flag.
